title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of the standard Tate–Deligne 'formulaire' for Weierstrass equations. The archive file contains typescript copies, and the section structure and numbering here (1.8, §2 'Cas où 2 et 3 sont inversibles', Prop. 2.5, then §3 'Cas où 2 et c4 sont inversibles') match Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476 (1975).

(1.8) Under a change of Weierstrass coordinates x = u^2x'+r, y = u^3y'+su^2x'+t (with π = uπ'), the quantities c4, c6 and Δ transform by u^4, u^6 and u^12. Equivalently, c4·π^{⊗4}, c6·π^{⊗6} and Δ·π^{⊗12} are well-defined sections of ω^{⊗4}, ω^{⊗6} and ω^{⊗12}. These are the modular forms of weight 4, 6 and 12 in Katz's sense.

§2: If 6 is invertible, then for a given π one can choose s, r, t uniquely to kill a1, a2, a3. This gives y^2 = x^3 + a4x + a6 with π = dx/2y. Here b2 = 0, b4 = 2a4, b6 = 4a6 and b8 = -a4^2, which yields c4 = -48a4, c6 = -864a6 and Δ = 16(-4a4^3 - 27a6^2).

Setting Y = 2y gives classical Weierstrass form Y^2 = 4X^3 - g2X - g3 with π = dX/Y. Then g2 = -4a4 = c4/12, g3 = -4a6 = c6/216 and Δ = g2^3 - 27g3^2.

Prop. 2.5: over Z[1/6], pairs (genus-one curve, invertible invariant differential) have fine moduli space Spec Z[1/6][g2, g3], with the universal Weierstrass curve. Since π is fixed, automorphisms (which act on π by roots of unity) are killed, so the pair is rigid. This serves the computation of the ring of modular forms Z[1/6][c4, c6] and the moduli of elliptic curves away from 2 and 3.
errors: Prop. 2.5 gives the moduli scheme as Spec Z[1/6][g2,g3]. That is correct for (possibly singular) Weierstrass cubics with a differential. For smooth genus-one curves (elliptic curves) one must invert Δ, giving Spec Z[1/6][g2,g3][Δ^{-1}]. Whether this is a gap depends on whether 'courbe de genre un' here allows nodal and cuspidal fibres.
Minor typos: 'Spec(Z[2^{-1},3^{-1}]' has an unbalanced parenthesis, and 'C, schéma' should read 'Ce schéma'.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript copy of Deligne's published Tate formulaire, with standard and correct computations that are well documented in the literature. Nothing in it is original to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'Ce schéma est' appears in the typescript as 'C, schéma est' (a typing defect).
The parenthesis after Spec is unclosed in the original: 'Spec(Z[2^{-1}, 3^{-1}]'.
